dossier_meta.subject: Graph Theory » Algebraic Graph Theory
dossier_meta.statement_text: Let $ \Phi(G,x) $ be the flow polynomial of a graph $ G $ . So for every positive integer $ k $ , the value $ \Phi(G,k) $ equals the number of nowhere-zero $ k $ -flows in $ G $ . Conjecture $ \Phi(G,5.5) > 0 $ for every 2-edge-connected graph $ G $ .
dossier_meta.context_text: By Seymour's 6-flow theorem, $ \Phi(G,k) > 0 $ for every 2-edge-connected graph $ G $ and every integer $ k\ge6 $ . It would be interesting to find any non-integer rational number $ x>5 $ so that $ \Phi(G,x) > 0 $ for every 2-edge-connected graph $ G $ . It is known that zeros of flow polynomials are dense in the complex plane.
